geometry.rounding: Nearest integer kilogram, halves up, of density times 50 ft^3. mu = that kilogram times proposalMuPerKg. A derived row rounds once from the parent's integer kilogram.

legacyHalfSlice.rule: A legacy save's stratum is half the height of one slice of the same square. Its mu is massPerSlice divided by 2. An odd mu gives the extra 1 to the upper half. This package does not migrate saves.

exemption.text: Items stored within active, claimed, or enclosed structures are exempt from reclamation.

disagreements.text: Lane Q uses integer kilograms, Lane R assumes 1 mu = 1/16 lb, Lane W uses grams, and the ledger leaves mu unset. This catalogue proposes 1 mu = 1 g (1000 mu per kg) so the Lane Q integers and the catalogue weight field both land on integers. The proposal is not confirmed.
Lane Q §9.1 splits soil 950 mineral / 50 organic. The ledger keeps soil mineral and humus organic so a transform never crosses families. The split is stored and not applied.
Lane R sends combustion gas to an AIR sink. The ledger has no such sink and keeps ash plus charcoal. The gas fraction is retained as charcoal. Lane R fractions are stored with applied:false.
DEC-028 sends wood, organics, corpses and bone to soil. The ledger rot and litter rows end at humus, not soil. Both are recorded. The applied ledger class is humus.
DEC-028 says stone and masonry rubble become solid stone. The ledger has no rubble-to-stone row. The applied path is weather to sediment, then lithify to stone.
DEC-028 allows metals to become rust, scrap or trace. Lane R NOBLE never corrodes, and the ledger has no gold or platinum trace class. Noble metal reclaims as scrap of the same class.

The catalogue has tin and bronze. The ledger has no sn family. Tin mass is unmapped. Bronze's 880/1000 copper share is cu_metal; the 120/1000 tin share is unmapped. The 88/12 split is Lane Q's example, a PM default.
The ledger has no bone class (LEDGER_API.md §10). Bone is booked as biomass and rots to humus.
Lane Q ash is 850 kg per slice (0.6 t/m3). Lane R's 40 lb/ft3 is a different slice mass. The Lane Q integer is the one used.
Lane Q gives no charcoal slice mass. Lane R's 15 lb/ft3 is converted by the kilogram rounding rule to 340 kg.
7 du per 10-ft layer does not divide by 5 slices. Per-slice water is null.
DEUS_ResourceRegistry.json salvageRecoveryRates.masonry_structures is 0.8. Lane Q cites a 75 percent return. Neither fraction is applied. Salvage returns the whole mass; nothing is deleted.
Catalogue object masses are the build bill or the conserving yield. They are not a count of Lane Q voxels. SIM.40.11 has to reconcile the two.
Several catalogue actions do not conserve mass (wall quarry that also leaves rubble, door dismantle that returns half, chop that drops hardware or fruit). Those counts are recorded and not applied.
gold_outcrop yields the gold item, which is booked as au_metal. The outcrop's mass is au_ore. The applied path is mine then smelt, equal mu, no new metal.
The rubble and rubble_pillar props yield stone in the catalogue. The applied yield stays class rubble (ledger pick).
The gravel prop's only yield is one stone item, so the prop is booked as stone. The strata material gravel is class rubble.
clay_deposit gather yields 2 clay and quarry yields 3, and both remove the prop. The quarry count is the applied mass.
The catalogue ruin of campfire is bones_pile. That is not applied. Collapse follows the log and stone bill.
timber_frame is described as organic plus mineral infill. The published kilogram figure is 0.12 of the species only. No infill mass is invented.
Lane Q debris of timber is broken_timber in place. The ledger has no wood object-to-strata row. Collapse is booked as salvage to a wood item of equal mass, named broken_timber.
Metal classes have no strata form. Loose scrap is booked as the metal item form.
LEDGER_API.md §9.2 calls trees biomass objects. Lane Q's trunk is wood, and the chop yield is wood. Trees are booked as wood. The hook text is not applied.

Lane R names glass, ceramic, lead and special metals. The ledger has no class for them. They are not given a stand-in class. Glass and ceramic decay lives are recorded only as class keys with no mass.
Snow is reserved. Class water has no snow form, so no ledger class is assigned.
Loose ice bulk is 607 kg, which is 0.6 of the 1,011 kg slice. A broken slice still deposits 1,011 kg.
